what: B1 loophole: a PR can edit the pin file instead of writing a decision file (the pin is the baseline). CI cannot see history in a shallow checkout
proposed_fix: add a CI step on pull_request with fetch-depth 0 that diffs tests/pins/defaults.json against the base branch and fails when an existing key's value changed or a key disappeared (additions only)

what: every session spends ~5 min building the torch environment by hand
proposed_fix: SessionStart hook (see the session-start-hook skill) that installs the CPU torch wheel and .[dev] into a venv

what: a ratchet that must also be lowered when it improves costs a round trip when two PRs both shrink the same count
proposed_fix: make test_rules_growth print the exact JSON line to paste (already lists the places); consider a --update script in tests/scan.py if conflicts appear

what: 'Add a CLAUDE.md line check that STATUS is < 60 lines' can mean 'add a line to CLAUDE.md' or 'add a check'; did both: CLAUDE.md now states the limit, tests/test_docs_claims.py reads and enforces it
proposed_fix: say which in the roadmap text

what: 'defined once (HeadSpec / schema)': there is no module named schema for output keys (core/schema.py is data columns). Chose model/heads.py as the home of output names
proposed_fix: name the module in the rule (done in tests/scan.py OUTPUT_NAME_HOME); consider moving the head vocabulary into core/

what: 'every module in a registry folder is registered' has no operational meaning when folders mix components and support code; defined as: registers something OR is imported by another module of src/. Result: 4 pinned orphans that are probably entry points
proposed_fix: decide at R-REVIEW whether entry points are exempt; list exempt modules with a reason like G3

what: header said 'No PyTorch code yet' (false since B1): fixed in this PR with a test. The OPEN list under it (items 1-10) was never re-triaged after the port; several are settled (see BUILD_PLAN.md) but I could not verify each
proposed_fix: owner or a docs step re-triages NOTES.md OPEN into RESOLVED / still open

what: target_cfg.get("loss_fn", "mse") and .get("huber_delta", 1.0) are silent config defaults, against rule B5; no check counts them
proposed_fix: add a ratchet for config .get(key, default) on config dicts (a G-style count) and move these defaults into a typed settings dataclass

what: 'PRs since last R-REVIEW' is a hand-kept counter; R-REVIEW is due after 5 merged PRs
proposed_fix: derive it from the STATUS tables (count of merged rows after the last review date) in a docs test

what: the caller must build the RunIdentity.settings_hash itself (test_fit does hash(asdict(FitSettings))); easy to forget a field (tasks config, model overrides) and then resume would not refuse a changed objective
proposed_fix: a helper that hashes FitSettings + trainer config + ModelSettings.overrides into the identity; fit(run_dir=...) then needs no hand-made identity (T3 runner is the place)

what: the lambda schedules dict is parsed twice with different strictness: __init__ reads c.get('start', 0.0) silently, fit parses ParamSchedule strictly (start and end required)
proposed_fix: parse config['loss']['schedules'] into ParamSchedule once in __init__ and keep the dict

what: seed_everything alone does not make resume equal an uninterrupted run (dropout masks and shuffle order depend on RNG position); I added a per-epoch reseed torch.manual_seed(seed*1_000_003+epoch), which changes the data order vs a plain seeded loop
proposed_fix: state in the roadmap that every random draw in the loop must be a function of (seed, epoch)

what: TF has more around the loop that T1 does not list: warm_start / lr rewarm, EpochGuard, EMA weights, grad clipping (B-018), TaskWeightUpdater, snapshot ensembles, Drive mirror. I ported none of them
proposed_fix: say in the roadmap which are out of scope for the baseline; B-018 tracks the optimizer ones

what: 'a new default needs a decision file' is only checkable for decisions that exist; a PR that pins new defaults and writes no decision still passes (pin additions are free)
proposed_fix: CI step comparing tests/pins/defaults.json with the base branch: every added key must appear in a decision file of the same PR (same step as the R0 suggestion for changed keys)

what: said only 'a default change needs a decision file'; the owner extended it to new defaults in the T1 prompt: fixed in this PR (RULES.md + docs/decisions/README.md)
no test connects the two sides of the artifact: I checked by hand that the TF tool's output on the fixture loads here (`--verify-hashes` OK); CI should do it
proposed_fix: a torch CI job that checks out TF at a pinned commit, runs tools/export_torch_artifact.py on tests/fixtures/tiny_dataset.dataset and loads the result with data_io/artifact.py

what: 'timestamp' is not said to be bar OPEN time or close time; the label-bar maths (ts + horizon x bar) and max_bar_time depend on it. I assumed open time from TF data/windows.py (base_index[end_idx])
proposed_fix: one line in core/schema.py and the contract doc stating the timestamp semantics, checked against the first Colab export

where: docs/ROADMAP.md T2 vs the session prompt
what: the RunIdentity builder and the identity.seed check in Trainer.fit are not in the ROADMAP T2 bullets (they came from the prompt), and T2 silently needs T1 merged
proposed_fix: add both bullets to T2 and 'needs T1' in the STATUS note

what: says the contract was recorded at TF aeafc564; the real export records the TF commit it ran on (and the lock only exists in later commits), so two commits now matter
proposed_fix: state in the header that the fixture is pinned at aeafc564 and a real artifact carries its own export.source_commit

what: 'PRs since last R-REVIEW: 1 (R0)' was stale after T1 merged: fixed in this PR (3 = R0, T1, T2)

where: TF CLAUDE.md 'Subagents' vs this repo's CLAUDE.md
what: TF CLAUDE.md says delegate large tasks to subagents by default, this repo says none; a session working on both gets conflicting instructions
proposed_fix: state in the session prompt (done by the owner here) or add 'unless the task prompt says otherwise' to the TF file

what: the TF CLAUDE.md lists the full suite as the only test command, but a new module is checked by repo-wide AST guards (tests/test_timeframe_normalize.py, tools/check_patterns.py) that only show up after ~23 min of CI
proposed_fix: add a `pytest -k 'guard or normalize or patterns'` line (a ~10 s subset of the repo-wide guards) to the TF CLAUDE.md Commands, to run before pushing a new package/tool file
